input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The new minimum wait defaults to one second instead of zero.
- failure path: With default options, an early exponential result below one second is raised to a one-second delay, slowing retries that previously had no configured floor.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new `min` parameter defaults to 1 instead of 0, so every existing `wait_exponential_jitter` user now gets a minimum wait of 1 second.
- rationale: Trigger: `wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.1, jitter=0)` or any config whose computed wait falls below 1s, with no `min` passed. The return `max(max(0, self.min), ...)` clamps the result up to 1, so waits shorter than 1s are silently lengthened. Callers see slower retries and changed timing; the previous behavior floored at 0.
critique: The finding identifies the same defect: the new min parameter defaults to 1 instead of 0. It also describes the same failure path, where exponential waits computed below one second are clamped up to one second, slowing retries compared with the previous zero floor.
